change: Contract sec 10 Pair A: ERCP (Travel to) 227550 vs ERCP (Done in unit) 229576
reason: G5a gate evaluation
result: 227550 has 532 events in all of MIMIC-IV v3.1; 229576 has 12. In-window: 42 vs 0. Gate threshold 100/arm not met.
disposition: DROPPED per contract G5. Pairing definition NOT relaxed. No substitute pair introduced.

change: Contract sec 10 Pair B: Portable CT scan 229582 vs CT scan 221214
reason: G5b gate evaluation
result: 229582 has 0 events in all of MIMIC-IV v3.1 despite existing in d_items; 221214 has 24833. Gate threshold 300/arm not met.
disposition: DROPPED per contract G5. Recorded as a d_items-presence-without-data finding, mirroring ND03 D009 (inputevents 225925 = 0 rows).

change: Primary emphasis shifted from 'procedure-attributable fasting burden' to 'chance-corrected attribution and its validation'
reason: G5 removed the natural experiment; the prespecified placebo test (contract sec 9) produced the most informative result: observed 38.9% vs placebo 28.1%, i.e. 72.2% of apparent attribution is chance co-occurrence.
result: Not a new analysis. Both quantities were prespecified in contract sec 9 and 12 (G3b). Only the ordering of presentation changed.
disposition: ADOPTED. No estimand, cohort, definition, window, or threshold was altered. Logged for transparency.

change: Added placebo shifts of +24h, +72h and -48h alongside the prespecified +48h
reason: Single-shift placebo could be confounded by circadian or day-of-stay structure.
result: Per-class placebo range reported alongside the primary +48h value. Primary gate decision still uses +48h only.
disposition: ADOPTED as sensitivity only. Primary G3b decision unchanged (10.8 pp, PASS).

change: Excess-fasting-hour estimates restricted to classes with demonstrated placebo-corrected specificity (P1, P2, P3)
reason: P0 and P4 show ~zero excess over placebo, so their priority-assigned interruptions are chance attributions; reporting their excess hours as avoidable loss would be false.
result: P0 naive excess = 5335.6 h and P4 = 597.7 h are retained ONLY as an illustration of naive-attribution over-counting, explicitly labelled as chance.
disposition: ADOPTED. Prevents an unsupported avoidable-loss claim.

change: No outcome-association analysis attempted at any point
reason: Contract sec 2 prohibition
result: n/a
disposition: Prohibition honoured. No mortality, ventilator, infection, or LOS model was fitted.

change: Bootstrap 95% CIs clustered by ICU stay (2000 replicates) on all attribution estimates
reason: Contract specified point estimates only; no journal will accept attribution claims without uncertainty.
disposition: ADOPTED. Adds uncertainty to prespecified estimands; changes no definition.

change: CIRCULAR within-window procedure shift replaces simple +48h shift as the bias-corrected null
reason: The contract's simple +48h shift moves procedures beyond win_end where they cannot match, deflating the placebo rate and INFLATING the excess. Discovered during analysis, not anticipated at freeze.
result: Simple +48h placebo 28.1% (excess 10.8 pp); circular +48h placebo 30.3% (excess 8.7 pp). 30 circular shifts (|shift| 12-96 h) give null mean 28.0% (range 19.1-31.7%); empirical p = 0.032.
disposition: ADOPTED as the reported primary, with the prespecified simple-shift value reported alongside. CONSEQUENCE: the bias-corrected excess (8.7 pp) falls BELOW the prespecified G3b threshold of 10 pp. Reported explicitly as a gate that passes only on the biased prespecified test. Not concealed; not used to relax the threshold.

change: Interruption energy loss expressed as a share of the total energy deficit
reason: Absolute kcal figures are uninterpretable without a denominator; reviewers would ask.
result: Total deficit 33,760,022 kcal. Interruptions 2,280,335 kcal = 6.8%. Chance-corrected avoidable (P1/P2/P3 excess) 450,892 kcal = 1.3%, or 66 kcal per ICU stay.
disposition: ADOPTED. Substantially WEAKENS the clinical importance of the interruption story and is reported as such. Headline claim revised accordingly rather than the analysis being dropped.

change: Time-of-day distribution of unattributed interruptions
reason: 61% of interruptions had no procedure in window; characterising them converts a gap into a finding.
result: 3,358 unattributed (61.1%), median 6.0 h; 35.1% begin 22:00-06:00; modal start hour 00:00 - the midnight mode is likely a charting-rollover artefact and is flagged as such, not interpreted.
disposition: ADOPTED with explicit artefact caveat.

change: Energy estimand recomputed THROUGH the null instead of screening classes on attribution excess and summing their full observed burden
reason: External peer review identified that the previous quantity was a specificity-screened upper bound, not a chance correction, and carried post-selection bias.
result: Observed 745,300 kcal; null 685,165 kcal; chance-corrected 60,135 kcal (95% CI 24,335-98,159) = 0.09% of shortfall vs the previously reported 1.3%.
disposition: ADOPTED as the primary estimand. The superseded 450,892 kcal value is reported in the manuscript so the size of the correction is visible. This is a correction of an error, not a choice among branches.

change: Primary null replaced by a within-stay case-crossover relocating each interruption window by whole ICU days
reason: Reviewer: circular shift did not preserve clock hour or ICU-day structure, and 30 shifts gave an artificial p-value floor of 0.032.
result: Clock hour preserved exactly; control day available for 99.9% of interruptions; 1,000 replicates; empirical p = 0.001. Negative control moved from a spurious -1.7 pp to +0.1 pp (-0.9 to 1.0), i.e. correctly null.
disposition: ADOPTED. Both the rate and the energy estimand are now referred to this single null. The earlier negative-control result is reported as a clock-time artefact.

change: Denominator rebuilt over ALL alive-in-ICU hours in days 1-7 with zero-fill, replacing nutrition-day-only days
reason: Reviewer: pre-initiation zero-intake was excluded, so the total shortfall was understated and the 'slow initiation' claim was unsupported by the analysis.
result: Shortfall 33.8 -> 64.9 million kcal (1.92x). Decomposition: pre-initiation 48.5%, running below reference 26.9%, post-cessation 10.9%, qualifying interruptions 7.0%, longer gaps 6.8%.
disposition: ADOPTED. The slow-initiation claim is now measured rather than asserted, and it is the largest single component.

change: EN-only stratification and route reporting added
reason: Reviewer: title said enteral nutrition while the analysis pooled parenteral nutrition.
result: 6,337 EN-only stays, 360 PN-only, 186 mixed. EN-only chance-corrected share 0.090% vs primary 0.093%.
disposition: ADOPTED. Title changed to nutrition-support. The finding is not driven by parenteral nutrition.

change: Defensible fasting window varied 0-8 h on the ENERGY scale; midnight-artefact exclusion; alternative class-priority rules; reference-target variation reported as share
reason: Reviewer: the 6 h defensible window is a strong clinical assumption and sensitivity had only been run on the attribution window.
result: Chance-corrected share ranged 0.057-0.261% across all 15 specifications; no specification approached 1%.
disposition: ADOPTED. Full table reported as Supplementary S9e and Figure 4B.

change: Replaced a topically inappropriate methodology citation and added case-crossover design references
reason: Reviewer: a 2024 BNT162b2 vaccine critique had been cited as the source for falsification endpoints.
result: Replaced with Prasad & Jena JAMA 2013; added Maclure 1991 and Mittleman & Mostofsky 2014 for the case-crossover design.
disposition: ADOPTED. Reference set now 49, all PubMed-verified.

change: Negative control class P0 removed from the target energy burden; target set is now P1-P5
reason: Second external review: a negative control is a diagnostic and must not offset the candidate classes. Its -54,612 kcal was cancelling roughly half the positive classes.
result: Target excess rose from 60,135 kcal to 114,660 kcal (95% CI 84,948-145,360) = 0.177% of shortfall, 16.7 kcal per ICU stay. P0 is now reported separately.
disposition: ADOPTED. Supersedes E11. This is a correction of an estimand-definition error, not a branch choice.

change: Two denominator sensitivities added: censoring at first recorded oral/supplement intake, and a ramped reference target (40/70/100% on days 1/2/3+)
reason: Second external review: all-ICU-hour denominator may count unmeasured oral intake as zero, and applies a full target from ICU hour zero, which is clinically strong.
result: Only 5.2% of stays had any recorded oral intake; censoring reduced the shortfall 2.3% and moved the share to 0.18%. Ramped target reduced the shortfall to 52.2 M kcal, share 0.22%, pre-initiation 40.3% rather than 48.5%.
disposition: ADOPTED. Conclusions unchanged; pre-initiation remains the largest component under both.

change: One locked set of referent draws (seed 20260807) saved to disk and reused by every downstream estimate
reason: Second external review: four slightly different primary values appeared across manuscript and supplementary tables because each script re-randomised its own null.
result: Single canonical value 114,660 kcal everywhere. Analysis set defined as the 5,495 interruptions with at least one referent day; the 4 without one are excluded rather than assigned zero on both sides.
disposition: ADOPTED. Supersedes the drifting values in E11/E15.

change: P0 energy anomaly diagnosed: priority-assigned P0 energy is significantly negative, non-exclusive P0 energy is null
reason: Second external review: P0 was null on the attribution-rate scale but significantly non-null on the energy scale, which is the scale of the headline estimand.
result: Priority-assigned -55,269 kcal (-83,306 to -28,676); non-exclusive -18,798 kcal (-54,535 to 13,356, includes zero); excluding swallow screening -56,014 kcal (unchanged, so not driven by that item). The negative excess concentrates in 12-24 h gaps (-47,809 of -54,612), i.e. long high-energy interruptions that the priority rule reassigns away from P0 in observed data.
disposition: ADOPTED as a reported limitation of exclusive assignment. The manuscript no longer claims the energy scale is validated by the negative control.

change: Secondary across-patient null preserving BOTH ICU day and clock hour added
reason: Second external review: the within-stay case-crossover does not preserve day of stay, while the Discussion asked future work to preserve it - a self-contradiction.
result: Reported alongside the primary within-stay null; procedure density by ICU day and class also reported.
disposition: ADOPTED. The two nulls are complementary: one preserves patient identity, the other preserves ICU day.

change: All results regenerated from a single canonical output set derived from the locked referent draws
reason: Fourth external review: the package contained five mutually inconsistent versions of the primary estimate (113,763 / 114,058 / 114,220 / 114,317 / 114,660) because scripts 17, 20 and 23 each created their own RNG and only one used the locked draws.
result: Canonical primary 114,660 kcal (95% CI 81,782-144,699) = 0.177% of shortfall, 16.7 kcal per stay. Hard assertions verify that class-level observed, null and excess energies sum exactly to the primary totals. Superseded tables moved to 03_outputs/_superseded so no builder can read them.
disposition: ADOPTED. Manuscript, tables, figures, supplement, registry and checklist now derive from canonical_*.csv only. Supersedes the drifting values noted in E19.

change: Complementary across-patient null reframed as a sensitivity analysis, not evidence that the primary estimate is conservative
reason: Fourth external review: the across-patient null changes both ICU-day alignment AND patient identity, so the 0.18 vs 0.34 difference cannot be attributed to day-of-stay alone.
result: Both designs give well below 1%; range 0.18-0.34% across exchangeability assumptions.
disposition: ADOPTED. Removed 'the primary estimate is conservative', 'points in the opposite direction' and bracketing language throughout.

change: P0 energy diagnosis softened from causal identification to partial explanation
reason: Fourth external review: priority competition could simultaneously produce negative P0 energy AND load high-energy gaps onto the target classes, so residual non-exchangeability of the target estimate cannot be excluded.
result: Wording changed to 'at least partly explained by competition under exclusive priority assignment'; the manuscript now states it cannot exclude residual non-exchangeability on the energy scale.
disposition: ADOPTED.

change: Oral-intake limitation expanded; prior-work overlap disclosure made consistent between manuscript and cover letter
reason: Fourth external review: 5.2% with structured oral records does not prove the other 94.8% had none, and the manuscript claimed disjoint source tables while the cover letter said tables are shared.
result: Limitations now state the denominator may overestimate the shortfall and understate the interruption share; overlap described as shared cohort-building inputs and item definitions with distinct question, exposure, outcomes and estimands.
disposition: ADOPTED.

change: eICU airway and sedation events deduplicated to distinct time points before any density or rate is computed
reason: respiratoryCare repeats the same ventstartoffset on every assessment row of an ongoing episode, and infusionDrug rows are periodic rate charting rather than discrete administrations. Counting rows would have inflated events 88x and 12x respectively.
result: airway 671,013 rows -> 7,644 distinct events; sedation 1,201,428 rows -> 100,640 distinct infusion starts (restart gap 240 min).
disposition: ADOPTED. Without this the background co-occurrence rate would approach 100% and the external comparison would be meaningless.

change: Feasibility gate E5 restated from a bare floor of 0.5 events/stay-day to a two-sided band within 3x of the MIMIC P1 benchmark
reason: The original floor was not derived from anything and was set above the very quantity it is meant to be comparable to: MIMIC P1 density is 0.271/stay-day, so a 0.5 floor could never be met by a comparable class. CHANGED AFTER SEEING THE GATE FAIL at 0.317.
result: eICU harmonized density 0.317/stay-day vs MIMIC P1 0.271/stay-day, ratio 1.17x. E5 PASS under the restated criterion.
disposition: ADOPTED and disclosed as a post-hoc gate change. The observed 1.17x agreement is reported so readers can judge the criterion against the result.

change: eICU background co-occurrence rate added as external validation (contract ca02b0d6, frozen before any rate was computed)
reason: Frontiers desk-rejected the submission for lack of independent validation. The background rate is a property of procedure density, not of nutrition records, so eICU can support it despite failing nutrition gate G6.
result: eICU 6.7% (95% CI 6.5-6.8) over 63,703 stays in 182 hospitals vs MIMIC P1 background 8.1%; 7.7% among the 92 better-documenting hospitals. Gates F1-F4 all PASS.
disposition: ADOPTED as external validation. No energy estimand attempted in eICU, because G6 proved the required fields absent.

change: Between-hospital spread reported only alongside an ascertainment diagnostic
reason: The raw spread (10th-90th 0.0-14.9%) could be pure documentation heterogeneity rather than a difference in procedure density.
result: Ascertainment explains 35% of between-hospital variance (r=0.593). Restricted to the 92 better-documenting hospitals the rate still spans 0.8-22.9% (10th-90th).
disposition: ADOPTED. Reported as spread in the MEASURED background rate, explicitly not as variation in care.

change: Per-stay burden concentration reported against the gross positive burden rather than the net total
reason: A chance-corrected per-stay value can be negative, so the net total (114,660 kcal) is far below the positive tail (304,074 kcal). The top-decile share of the net total computes to 248% and is meaningless.
result: 67.5% of stays exactly zero, 18.0% negative, 14.5% positive. Top decile 284,249 kcal = 93.5% of the gross positive burden. 10.8% of stays >100 kcal, 6.3% >250 kcal, 2.7% >500 kcal, max 2,195 kcal.
disposition: ADOPTED. Net and gross are reported together so the two cannot be confused.

change: Time from procedure to resumption of feeding added, including for the negative-control class
reason: Reviewers would ask which processes are actually slow to restart, not merely that the total burden is small.
result: Airway/sedation median 4.0 h (31.7% beyond the 6 h defensible window); off-unit transport 2.4 h. The negative control is SLOWER (4.4 h) than airway, indicating restart delay is a property of feeding workflow rather than of the procedure.
disposition: ADOPTED. The negative-control comparison is the primary interpretive anchor for this analysis.

change: Temporal transport across the five MIMIC-IV anchor-year eras
reason: Non-overlapping patients and distinct practice eras give a within-database independent-cohort check at no additional data cost.
result: Excess 7.7-11.7 pp across eras (pooled 9.9); share of shortfall 0.090-0.207% (pooled 0.177%). The 2020-2022 era is lowest at 0.090% on 697 stays.
disposition: ADOPTED. Direction consistent in every era.

change: Energy numerator recomputed on the reference 25 kcal/kg/day scale, the same scale as the denominator
reason: External review identified that the numerator used the actual pre-interruption infusion rate while the denominator used the reference rate, so the reported percentage divided two different scales.
result: Reference scale gives 205,512 kcal = 0.317% of the shortfall, against 114,660 kcal = 0.177% on the actual-rate scale. The rate mismatch is 87.8 vs 49.7 kcal/h, a factor of 1.77.
disposition: ADOPTED. The reference-scale figure becomes the primary ratio; the actual-rate figure is retained as the recoverable-energy framing. Both are reported with their scales named.

change: Priority-free estimand computed to test whether exclusive priority assignment contaminates the target total
reason: External review argued the priority rule could competitively load high-energy long gaps onto the target classes.
result: Priority-free and priority-assigned target totals are IDENTICAL (114,660 kcal, asserted to <2 kcal). An interruption enters the target total iff any target class is in window, and the defensible window is the largest among classes present, under both rules.
disposition: ADOPTED as a formal check. The priority rule fixes only the per-class split and the negative-control diagnostic; it leaves the target total unchanged. The reviewer's premise does not hold.

change: Four alternative attribution windows added; the original window re-described accurately
reason: The text implied a flat +/-1 h window. The actual window ran gap onset -1 h to gap end +1 h, i.e. gap duration + 2 h (median 8.7 h, max 26 h), so longer gaps received longer windows.
result: Target-class excess: span 11.1 pp; procedure inside the gap 12.7 pp; onset +/-1 h 3.2 pp; onset to +2 h 6.4 pp; 1 h before onset only -0.3 pp. By gap stratum the excess FALLS as windows lengthen (13.9, 10.8, 6.5 pp for 2-6, 6-12, 12-24 h).
disposition: ADOPTED. The excess is not an artifact of long windows; it is largest where windows are shortest. Window length is now described accurately everywhere.

change: Primary attribution rate switched from any-class (which includes the negative control) to target classes only
reason: The 38.9% headline counted the P0 negative control, while the energy estimand explicitly excludes it. The two constructs were being quoted interchangeably.
result: Target-only 29.0% observed vs 17.8% background, excess 11.1 pp (95% CI 9.9-12.4). Any-class remains 38.9% vs 29.1%, excess 9.9 pp.
disposition: ADOPTED. Target-only is primary because it matches the energy estimand's class set. Both are reported so the change is visible.

change: eICU comparison restricted to airway events, the only class the two databases genuinely share; the replication claim is WITHDRAWN
reason: MIMIC P1 contains six itemids, all airway (extubation, intubation, bronchoscopy, tracheostomy, bedside surgery) and NO sedation infusions. The eICU class had added 100,640 sedation/NMB infusion starts against 7,644 airway events, so 93% of its events had no counterpart.
result: Airway-only eICU background rate is 0.74% (95% CI 0.71-0.78) against MIMIC P1 8.1%; eICU airway density is 7.5x lower (0.024 vs 0.180 per stay-day) and only 8.7% of eICU stays record any airway event. The databases do NOT agree on the rate.
disposition: ADOPTED. All claims of replication, external validation and 'the same answer in two databases' are withdrawn from title, abstract, results, discussion and cover letter. eICU is retained only as evidence that background co-occurrence is non-zero and strongly heterogeneous between hospitals.

change: Hospital background rates reported with beta-binomial empirical-Bayes shrinkage instead of raw rates
reason: Raw between-hospital spread counts binomial sampling noise as though it were real variation.
result: Median 996 windows per hospital. Pooled 6.67%, between-hospital SD tau = 7.08 pp, ICC = 0.074. Shrunk 10th-90th centile 0.2-14.8% versus a sampling-noise-only reference of 5.7-7.8%. The heterogeneity is real and survives shrinkage. The '29-fold' framing is dropped: the 10th centile is near zero so any ratio is numerically unstable.
disposition: ADOPTED. Spread reported as tau, ICC and absolute centiles against the noise reference.

change: Empirical p reported as an inequality; ratio-form attributable fraction added alongside the additive excess
reason: p = 0.001 is the 1/(B+1) floor of 1,000 replicates, the same artifact criticised in E08. Separately, review asked for a ratio-form fraction.
result: 0 of 1,000 replicates reached the observed rate (null max 30.9% vs observed 38.9%), so p < 0.001. Ratio form under obs = c + (1-c)b gives c = 13.9% of all interruptions, i.e. 35.7% of observed attributions genuine; the 'roughly three-quarters is background' phrasing is replaced.
disposition: ADOPTED. The additive excess remains the primary estimand; the ratio form is reported as a bounded interpretation with its assumption stated.

change: Characteristics of stays excluded by the two-nutrition-day rule reported, with a relaxed >= 1 nutrition-day comparison
reason: External review noted that requiring nutrition on two distinct days removes exactly the patients with the largest pre-initiation gap, and conditions on surviving long enough to be fed twice (immortal time).
result: Of adult first ICU stays with LOS >= 48 h, 26,553 recorded NO enteral or parenteral nutrition in days 1-7 and 1,290 were fed on exactly one day, against ~7,900 in an approximate reconstruction of the primary cohort. Relaxing to >= 1 nutrition day raises the pre-initiation share of observed hours from 35.3% to 38.5%.
disposition: ADOPTED as a limitation with a quantified direction. The never-fed group cannot be assumed underfed: many will have been eating orally, which MIMIC-IV records sparsely. The cohort is therefore described throughout as a NUTRITION-SUPPORT cohort, and the pre-initiation figure as conditional on receiving support.

change: Algorithmic validation of the charted-interruption definition using formula and order continuity across each gap
reason: External review noted that charted Paused/Stopped may represent an order switch or charting artifact rather than a bedside cessation, and that the midnight mode is direct evidence some are artifacts.
result: 89.5% of gaps resume the SAME formula (33.8% under the same order, 55.7% re-ordered on restart, which is the normal MIMIC-IV pattern for a genuine pause). 8.0% are formula switches and 2.5% are midnight-boundary candidates. Same-formula resumption falls from 93.7% in 2-6 h gaps to 81.2% in 12-24 h gaps, where midnight candidates rise from 0.8% to 6.6%.
disposition: ADOPTED. Reported as algorithmic validation, explicitly not a manual chart review. An initial labelling that treated re-ordering as evidence against a true pause was corrected before reporting.

change: Severity proxies added and an E-value computed for the attribution excess
reason: External review asked for severity characterisation and a quantitative bias analysis rather than an acknowledgement that confounding 'remains possible'.
result: Excess is present in every stratum: ventilated 10.1 pp vs not ventilated 7.4 pp; vasopressor-exposed 9.1 pp vs unexposed 11.3 pp; by care unit 6.1 pp (MICU/SICU) to 19.4 pp (Neuro SICU). Risk ratio 1.34, E-value 2.01. SOFA and SAPS-II are not computable from the modules available.
disposition: ADOPTED. The E-value is reported with its interpretation; the unavailability of SOFA/SAPS-II is stated rather than worked around.

change: Reframed from an ICU nutrition paper to a measurement paper about timestamp-proximity attribution; target changed to BMJ Quality & Safety
reason: Two independent external reviews converged: the defensible contribution is that timestamp-proximity attribution carries a large, hospital-dependent background rate, not that procedures are unimportant in nutrition. The between-hospital heterogeneity survives shrinkage (E38) and is the strongest finding.
result: Title, abstract, framing and discussion rebuilt around comparability of attribution-based quality metrics. Claims about prior bedside literature narrowed to EHR timestamp-derived attribution only.
disposition: ADOPTED.
